question: Can I fly my drone in High Park?
key_fact: Operating a drone in a City park is not allowed without a permit.
answer: Under By-law 1482-2025, in force 2026-03-02, the rule for drones is that while in a park, no person shall operate a drone, rocket or remote-controlled vehicle unless authorized by permit [2][4]. Before that date the consolidated text barred operating powered models of aircraft, rockets, watercraft or vehicles without a permit [1]. A drone is a remotely piloted aircraft system as defined in the Canadian Aviation Regulations [4]. So flying a drone in High Park requires a City permit. The passages do not say whether High Park issues drone permits or how to get one.

question: My contractor wants to start drilling at 7:30 on a Saturday. Is that allowed?
key_fact: No — audible construction noise is prohibited before 9 a.m. on Saturdays.
answer: Construction noise that is clearly audible is prohibited from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m. the next day, except until 9 a.m. on Saturdays, and all day Sundays and statutory holidays [1]. So drilling that is clearly audible at 7:30 a.m. on a Saturday is not permitted under the noise by-law, since the Saturday exception only runs until 9 a.m. [1]. The Infill notice also states that construction noise in residential areas is permitted only Monday to Friday 7am to 7pm and Saturday 9am to 7pm [2]. The passages do not address whether the drilling is a power device or construction equipment under every circumstance, or any exemption for a particular site.

question: My apartment is freezing. How warm does my landlord have to keep it?
key_fact: The landlord must keep at least 21 °C.
answer: Today, a landlord must maintain a minimum air temperature of 21 degrees Celsius at 1.5 metres above the floor in all areas of a rented dwelling unit from October 1 to May 15 of the following year, but only where the unit is normally heated at the landlord's expense. [1] This rule is in Chapter 497 and is already in force. From 2027-05-01, By-law 1512-2025 is set to replace Chapter 629 so that every residential unit must have a heating system capable of maintaining 21 degrees Celsius in all living spaces, including bathrooms and toilet rooms. [2] [3] The documents do not cover how a tenant enforces these requirements.

question: How long do I have to shovel the sidewalk after it snows?
key_fact: Within 12 hours after the snowfall has stopped.
answer: Under Chapter 719, an owner or occupant of a building must clear and completely remove snow and ice from the sidewalk on the highway in front of, alongside or at the rear of the building within 12 hours after the snowfall has ceased [1]. This does not apply where the City has taken on sidewalk clearing under City policy at that location [1]. question: How long can I leave my car running while I wait for someone?
key_fact: No more than one minute in any sixty-minute period.
answer: No person shall cause or permit a vehicle to idle for more than one minute in a sixty-minute period [1]. Idling is exempt where it is required to repair the vehicle or prepare it for service, for emergency vehicles, transit vehicles while passengers embark or disembark, and a few other listed cases, none of which is simply waiting for someone [1]. question: How many dogs am I allowed to have?
key_fact: Three dogs per dwelling unit.
answer: In a dwelling unit you may keep no more than three dogs, with grandfathering for dogs lawfully kept before the chapter's passage and an exception for service animals required by a person with a disability [1]. A dwelling unit is a room or group of rooms occupied as a home by one or more persons, with only one kitchen [7]. In a park, no person may have control of more than six dogs, and more than three requires a commercial dog walker permit [3]. Off your premises, a dog must be on a leash of no more than two metres unless in a designated off-leash area [2]. Every dog owner must also license each dog [5]. The passages do not cover any limit on dogs at a pet establishment beyond the rules above.

question: We're renovating. What hours can the crew work, and can they leave their trucks idling?
key_fact: Audible construction noise is not allowed from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m. (to 9 a.m. on Saturdays).
answer: Construction noise: construction or operation of construction equipment that is clearly audible is prohibited from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m. the next day, except until 9 a.m. on Saturdays, and all day on Sundays and statutory holidays [3]. Construction equipment includes hand tools, power tools, compressors, excavators, cranes and similar machines [8]. Idling: no person may cause or permit a vehicle to idle for more than one minute in any sixty-minute period [1]. Exemptions include vehicles where idling is required to repair the vehicle or prepare it for service, and vehicles required to remain motionless due to traffic, weather or mechanical difficulties beyond the operator's control [1]. The Infill notice standard also refers to working hours of Monday to Friday 7am to 7pm and Saturday 9am to 7pm, but that applies to the Infill notice content, not the noise rule itself [4]. The passages do not state whether a crew's own trucks count as construction equipment, so that point is not covered.

question: What does 591-2.1 say?
key_fact: It limits amplified or instrument sound measured at a point of reception.
answer: Section 591-2.1 bans emitting amplified or instrument sound that exceeds set decibel limits at an outdoor point of reception in a living area: 50 dB(A) or 65 dB(C) from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m., and 55 dB(A) or 70 dB(C) from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. [1]. Where ambient sound is already above those limits, the sound may not equal or exceed the ambient level [1]. If an officer finds outdoor measurement unreasonable, indoor limits of 42 dB(A)/57 dB(C) at night and 50 dB(A)/65 dB(C) by day apply instead [1]. The 2024 amendment added instrument sound to the rule [1]. The passages do not cover the definition of living area or point of reception.

question: My building has air conditioning. Does my landlord have to actually run it in summer?
key_fact: An installed cooling system must keep the indoor temperature at or below 26 °C.
answer: Yes. Under the current Chapter 629 rule, air-conditioning systems must be operated from June 1 to September 30 so as to maintain an indoor temperature of not more than 26 degrees Celsius [3]. Chapter 497 likewise requires every owner, operator and landlord to operate any installed cooling system in that period to keep indoor temperature at or below 26 degrees Celsius, and it applies to properties with existing air conditioning [1][7]. Note that By-law 67-2026 deleted subsection 629-38F, effective 2026-06-01, so the Chapter 629 operating requirement is removed from that date, while the Chapter 497 requirement still applies [6][1]. The documents do not cover whether the Chapter 629 replacement due 2027-05-01 keeps an equivalent operating duty, though its draft text does include one [2].

question: What did the City decide about electricity and its climate commitments in December 2025?
key_fact: The committee referred the item to the Executive Director without making a decision.
answer: On December 17, 2025, City Council adopted item IE26.3 with amendments, directing staff to include in the 'Electrification Advantage' report a plan to improve affordability, air quality and climate pollution and avoid unnecessary gas combustion at the Portlands Energy Centre by significantly increasing local distributed energy generation and storage and off-peak demand measures, above the IESO's 2025 minimums [3]. Council also directed staff to include opportunities to exceed the IESO's projections for distributed energy resources [4]. Council also endorsed Bill S-238 in principle and forwarded the item to the Senate [3]. Separately, on December 4, 2025, the Infrastructure and Environment Committee only referred item IE26.14 (Councillor Saxe's letter opposing the IESO's draft plan as incompatible with Toronto's climate commitments) to the Executive Director, Environment, Climate and Forestry, with no decision on its recommendations [2]. The documents do not cover the IESO's own plan or the Toronto Hydro and Auditor General requests from that letter's motion beyond that referral.

question: What's the City's position on the new e-bike rules?
key_fact: Council supported Ontario's proposed two-class e-bike definition (32 km/h, 500 W, working pedals, minimum age 16, helmets).
answer: City Council asked Transportation Services to submit comments to Ontario's Environment Registry supporting the province's proposed two-class definition for power-assisted bicycles: speed-limited to 32 km/h, 500 watts or less, functional pedals or hand cranks, no footrest, adjustable saddle, minimum operator age of 16, passengers allowed in a seat, and helmets required for all operators [1]. Council also asked for a 55 kg maximum weight limit for Class 2 power-assisted bicycles and brakes that can stop the vehicle within 9 metres even when loaded and in wet or hilly conditions [1]. The faster, heavier moped, scooter or motorcycle-style vehicles would be required to be licenced and insured under the proposal Council supported [1][2]. Council adopted these positions on May 21, 2026, with amendments [1]. The passages do not state whether the province has adopted these rules.
